label: Confirmed Cases (2026 DRC + Uganda + France)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker (updated 6 September) / DRC Ministry of Health — data as of 5 September 2026
contestNote: ECDC's tracker (updated 6 September, data as of 5 September) put DRC's confirmed toll at 6,604 cases and 3,175 deaths across 61 of 151 health zones in 6 provinces, an increase of 82 cases and 41 deaths from the prior report. DRC's own National Institute of Public Health (INSP) reported a slightly lower same-week figure (6,522 cases / 3,134 deaths as of 6 September) reflecting reconciliation lag between the two trackers. Uganda's outbreak was declared officially over 28 July 2026 by its own Ministry of Health (20 confirmed, 18 recoveries, 2 deaths) and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after completing the 42-day monitoring period. France: 1 case, recovered and discharged 4 July, no secondary transmission. Africa CDC officials warned 22 August that the true case count may be 2-3x higher (10,000-15,000) given official detection captures an estimated 30-40% of infections, and that transmission may have begun as early as February 2026, months before the 15 May declaration.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed cases roughly seventeenfold since early June: 400 (June 5) → 2,011 (July 15) → 3,605 (July 30) → 4,053 (August 5) → 4,665 (August 13) → 4,945 (August 16) → 5,021 (August 18) → 5,290 (August 20) → 5,584 (August 23) → 5,713 (August 25) → 5,794 (August 27) → 6,041 (August 31) → 6,186 (August 31 report, published 2 September) → 6,342 (2 September report, published 4 September) → 6,604 (5 September report, published 6 September; ECDC). This is now the largest Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second-largest ever recorded worldwide, behind only the 2014-16 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases). WHO's 100-day assessment (24 August) recorded an average of nearly 90 new confirmed cases per day over the outbreak's first three months; Forbes (27 August) put the doubling time at roughly 2.2 weeks, faster than West Africa's 5.3 weeks. WHO Director-General Tedros warned 2 September that up to 80% of new cases fall outside known contact lists — 'chains of transmission we don't know about' — and appealed for accelerated funding toward DRC's $1.3 billion six-month response plan, formally launched as a revised 180-day plan in Kinshasa on 4 September.

label: Deaths (2026 Outbreak)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 5 September 2026 (updated 6 September)
contestNote: Confirmed deaths: 3,175 DRC + 2 Uganda = 3,177 total as of 5 September (ECDC tracker, updated 6 September), a crude CFR of roughly 48.1%. DRC's own INSP reported a slightly lower same-week figure (3,134 deaths as of 6 September) reflecting reconciliation lag between the two trackers. The toll continues climbing, having already surpassed the 2,299 deaths of DRC's 2018-2020 Kivu outbreak to become the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history. WHO's 100-day review found roughly 60% of weekly deaths recorded in the prior six weeks occurred in communities outside treatment centers; Tedros warned 2 September that up to 80% of new cases fall outside known contact lists. A 7 September response-monitoring report found unclaimed, untested bodies peaking at 42 in a single day in Ituri before declining to 7-11 daily, and one body forcibly removed from a Haut-Uélé treatment center without testing.
deltaNote: DRC confirmed deaths: 64 (June 5) → 754 (July 15) → 1,587 (July 30) → 1,850 (August 5) → 2,184 (August 13) → 2,325 (August 16) → 2,378 (August 18) → 2,516 (August 20) → 2,680 (August 23) → 2,744 (August 25) → 2,786 (August 27) → 2,911 (August 31) → 3,007 (August 31 report, published 2 September) → 3,072 (2 September report, published 4 September) → 3,175 (5 September report, published 6 September; ECDC). 155-160 confirmed cases among healthcare workers; Forbes (27 August) cited 44-50 deaths (~29-32% CFR among HCWs). Over 40 healthcare workers killed and treatment centers/ambulances attacked per UN Secretary-General Guterres's 27 August Security Council briefing; a North Kivu community threatened 4 September to burn down a treatment center under construction in Katwa.

label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
value: ~48.1% (DRC, crude, as of 5 Sept); ~66% in North Kivu province
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 5 September 2026 (updated 6 September)
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to a peak near 48.6% in late August and stood at roughly 48.1% as of 5 September (6,604 cases / 3,175 deaths). Province-level variation remains stark: North Kivu (roughly 1,000 cases / 659 deaths as of 5 September) sits near 66%, well above the national average, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior. Africa CDC warned 22 August that if the official case count captures only 30-40% of true infections, the true CFR could be substantially lower than the crude reported figure. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — 70,000 Ervebo Doses Allocated, Phase 3 Trial Slips to October/November
value: 70,000 Ervebo doses released to DRC (20,000 for Phase 3 trial + 50,000 for frontline/health workers); human trial timeline has slipped from a mid-September target to October or November
source: WHO / Africa CDC / ICG / STAT News / Healio / medicalxpress — 12 August–2 September 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. WHO cautioned 'it is not known whether Ervebo may be protective against the Bundibugyo virus in humans,' though early lab/animal data suggest possible partial protection. WHO/DRC talks had targeted a mid-September launch as of 21 August, but WHO vaccines chief Kate O'Brien said 2 September the trial 'should begin by October or November,' with Ervebo likely first into the trial given its existing licensure; Tedros noted two additional candidates (Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV in the UK and a Moderna mRNA candidate in Canada) remain in earlier-stage safety trials. As of July, 16,250 Ervebo doses had already been distributed to frontline workers under compassionate use in Kisangani, Tshopo province. Animal data: 3/4 vaccinated primates survived BDBV challenge vs 1/4 controls; a ferret study showed 100% protection with a research-grade formulation vs 0% in controls.
delta: Phase 3 human trial start pushed from a mid-September target (reported 21 August) to October/November (reported 2 September)
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, and the slip to an October/November target are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway rather than a resumption of off-label ring vaccination. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 6 DRC provinces (61 health zones) + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker — data as of 5 September 2026 (updated 6 September)
delta: 61 of 151 health zones as of 5 September, up from 60 in late August — one additional health zone added while case counts within existing zones (notably Ituri and North Kivu) continue to climb
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of cases and deaths (5,326 cases / 2,398 deaths across 28 of 36 health zones as of 5 September). North Kivu (roughly 1,000 cases / 659 deaths across 16 of 34 zones, including Katwa, Biena and Manguredjipa) has the highest fatality rate of any affected province. Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six affected provinces; Bas-Uélé borders Central African Republic conflict-displacement corridors and has poor road/communications access. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over by its own Ministry of Health on 28 July and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after the 42-day monitoring period. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic. A 7 September response-monitoring report flagged 10 of 24 mapped health areas in Haut-Uélé and a community threat to burn a treatment center under construction in North Kivu's Katwa health zone as active resistance zones slowing containment.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker / response-monitoring report — data as of 5 September 2026
delta: National coverage held just above the 85% operational threshold at 85.7% (5 September), down slightly from ~88% (31 August), with sharp provincial disparities now documented for the first time
deltaNote: ECDC's tracker reported active follow-up at 85.7% of identified contacts nationally as of 5 September, versus 88% on 31 August. A 7 September response-monitoring report broke this down by province for the first time: Ituri leads at 89.8%, above the operational threshold, while North Kivu (83.3%), Tshopo (73.9%), Haut-Uélé (72.1%) and Bas-Uélé (69.7%) all lag behind it. WHO's 100-day assessment noted tracing coverage had climbed dramatically from just 9% in the outbreak's first week. A recalibrated Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69.3%, prompting a WHO/UNMISS preparedness mission to the border town of Ezo (27-28 August); no confirmed South Sudan case has been reported as of 7 September. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following its outbreak-end declaration, confirmed by WHO on 25 August. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone, and community resistance (isolation refusals, a patient escape in Katwa, blocked ring-closure in Tshopo) is separately undermining follow-up in several provinces.
